cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where server-side operations (returning privileged objects, evaluating dynamic code) are performed without proper authorization checks on user privileges or session origin. Attackers can exploit missing programming or script rights checks to escalate privileges, or lack of CSRF tokens to forge requests on behalf of authenticated users.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 8 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add explicit privilege check (e.g., hasProgrammingRights()) before returning the raw object or executing the method.
sub_patterns.name: Missing privilege check on raw object retrieval
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code assumes lower-level script right is sufficient for accessing raw objects that require programming right.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Wrap the internal object in its public API facade (e.g., new Attachment(...)) before returning to the scripting layer.
sub_patterns.name: Returning raw internal objects without access-controlled wrapper
sub_patterns.root_cause: Script service methods return internal domain objects directly, bypassing the API wrapper that enforces authorization checks.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add authorization check (hasAccess(Right.SCRIPT)) before evaluation; optionally restrict evaluation to safe properties or escape output.
sub_patterns.name: Missing script rights check before Velocity template evaluation
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled content (object properties, headings, UI extension parameters) is passed to Velocity #evaluate() without verifying that the content author has script rights, allowing arbitrary code execution.

sub_patterns.name: Missing authorization checks on privileged API methods and dynamic code evaluation
